title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: GAR 3 — 'enter' as begin-to-be; tip before PLAC reply
pass_a_gloss: GAR 3: What is said to be introduced often means what then first begins to be—as among the Greeks εἰς τὸ δικαστήριον εἰσελθεῖν, to enter into judgment, is to begin a suit. And Christ is said to have entered and been introduced into the world when he began to be in the world according to his humanity (Acts 1:21; Heb 1:6). Therefore when sin first began to be in the human race—through the first parents' disobedience—it is rightly said to have entered the world. Tip before PLAC's reply.
pass_b_english: GAR. 3. What is often said to be introduced is that which then at last begins to be, as among the Greeks eis to dikasterion eiselthein, to enter into judgment, is to begin a suit. And Christ is said to have entered, and to have been introduced into the world, when in the world he began to be according to his humanity. Acts 1. 21. Heb. 1. 6. Therefore when sin first began to be in the human race, which was through the first parents' disobedience, it is rightly said to have entered into the world.
source_text: GAR. 3. Quod sine introduci dicitur saepius, quod tum demum esse incipit, ut apud Graecos εἰς τὸ δικαστήριον εἰσελθεῖν intrare in iudicium, est incipere litem. Et Christus dicitur intrasse, & introductus fuisse in mundum, cum in mundo incepit esse secundum humanitatem suam. Act. 1. 21. Heb. 1. 6. Ergo cum peccatum incepit esse primum in genere humano, quod fuit per primorum parentum inobedientiam, merito dicitur in mundum intrasse.
